memos.headline: XOM at 52-week highs dominates relative strength; MSFT and UNH in structural downtrends
memos.body: I see a broad market under pressure—most names in our universe are 5-10% below their 50-day means and RSIs cluster in the 30-41 range—but the dispersion is enormous. XOM is the standout, sitting at its 52-week high with +40.4% 12-week relative strength vs SPY, +31.8% above its 200-day mean, and RSI 67.5 that is strong but not yet extreme; trend-following discipline says stay long until a close below the 50-day mean (~$145) signals exhaustion. GOOGL and CAT also trade well above their 200-day means (+15.8% and +27.5% respectively) with positive 12-week relative strength, though both have pulled back sharply over the last four weeks, so I want to see stabilization before adding. MSFT is the clearest avoid: down 29.6% from its 52-week high, 20.7% below its 200-day mean, RSI 32, and -16% relative strength over 12 weeks—this is a broken trend, and I would need a sustained reclaim of the 200-day (~$480) to reconsider. UNH's 54% drawdown from its high is catastrophic and structurally impaired; PG just printed RSI 30.9 with a -10.3% four-week return, which looks like capitulation but lacks any positive relative-strength signal to lean on.

views.note: At 52-week highs with dominant relative strength (+40% vs SPY over 12w); would reassess on a close below ~$145 (50-day area).
Well above 200-day mean (+15.8%) with positive 12w relative strength (+2.5% vs SPY); pullback to RSI 41 offers entry if $290 holds.
Massive 26w gain (+57.8%) and strong 200-day premium, but sharp 4w selloff (-10.4%) and -4.5% relative strength near-term warrant patience; watch $660 support.

Negative relative strength (-6% over 12w) and 4.9% below 200-day mean; bounce this week is encouraging but insufficient—watch $295 resistance.

memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; UNH's Near-Zero Margin Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I am most convicted on the durability of earnings at NVDA and MSFT. NVDA's FY2026Q4 10-K shows $68.13B in quarterly revenue (+73.2% YoY) with a 63.1% net margin and only $8.47B in total debt—this is extraordinary operating leverage with minimal balance-sheet risk. MSFT posted $81.27B in revenue (+16.7% YoY) with a 47.3% net margin and net income growth of 59.5%, suggesting cloud mix-shift is driving durable margin expansion. On the other end, UNH's 2025Q4 10-K is alarming: despite $113.22B in revenue (+12.3% YoY), net income collapsed to $0.01B—a 99.8% YoY decline—implying severe cost or reserve pressures that could persist. GOOGL's 18% revenue growth and 30.3% net margin on a clean $14.79B debt load also stand out favorably, while XOM's declining revenue (-1.3%) and 14.6% net income drop signal cyclical headwinds I do not want to own into.

views.note: 73% revenue growth, 63% net margin, and only $8.5B debt make this the strongest earnings-power profile in the universe.
47.3% net margin with 59.5% net income growth and moderate $40B debt signals durable, expanding earnings power from cloud mix.
18% revenue growth, 30.3% net margin, and low $14.8B debt provide a clean fundamental setup; I'd revisit if ad revenue decelerates.
$143.8B revenue (+15.7%) and 29.3% net margin are solid, though $88.5B total debt is the highest in the tech cohort and warrants monitoring.
Revenue growth of 13.6% is healthy but net income grew only 5.9% on a 9.9% margin, suggesting heavy reinvestment is compressing near-term cash earnings.
7.1% revenue growth is respectable for a bank but net income fell 7% YoY; I need to see provision trends before getting constructive.
Only 1.5% revenue growth and a 6.7% net income decline suggest limited pricing power; stable but uninspiring earnings trajectory.
18% revenue growth is strong but net income fell 13.9%, implying margin compression from input costs or mix; need to see operating cash flow detail.
Net income of $0.01B on $113B revenue is a near-total margin wipeout (-99.8% YoY); until the source of the collapse is clarified, this is uninvestable.
Revenue declined 1.3% and net income fell 14.6% with a 7.9% margin, reflecting commodity cyclical pressure I don't want to own.

memos.headline: Fed Pausing at 3.75% With Sticky Inflation and Rising Long Rates — Favor Defensives Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75bp of cuts over the prior year, and the February CPI print shows 2.4% YoY inflation that is still above target with a 0.7% three-month gain suggesting re-acceleration risk. Unemployment at 4.4% is benign (down 10bp over three months) so there is no labor-market urgency to cut further. The 10y yield has risen 23bp over three months to 4.39%, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 22bp to +46bp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and possibly slower growth ahead. This combination — paused Fed, sticky inflation, rising long-end yields, flattening curve — is a headwind for long-duration growth equities and a modest positive for banks' net interest margins, while defensive staples should hold up. A CPI print breaking convincingly below 2% or unemployment spiking above 4.7% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Long-duration equity faces headwinds from rising 10y yields and a paused Fed, but strong cash flows limit downside.
Highest-duration name in the universe is most vulnerable to the 23bp rise in 10y yields and no near-term rate relief.
Quality growth with recurring revenue cushions the blow, but higher-for-longer rates cap multiple expansion.
Consumer spending resilient given low unemployment, but rising discount rates weigh on forward earnings multiples.
Positive 10y-2y spread of 46bp and stable short rates support NIM; solid labor market limits credit losses.
Defensive staple benefits from late-cycle positioning; modest inflation pass-through supports pricing power.
Macro data shows no clear recession signal but no strong growth impulse either; energy lacks a directional catalyst from rates alone.
Cyclical bellwether faces risk from curve flattening (-22bp in 3m) which historically presages slower industrial activity.
Ad revenue tied to nominal GDP which is supported by 2.4% CPI, but higher long rates limit re-rating potential.
Defensive healthcare with pricing power in a sticky-inflation, pause-regime environment; less rate-sensitive than growth tech.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: UNH and MSFT Washouts May Be Turning, AMZN Filing Cluster Signals Ongoing Narrative Risk
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and subsequent 8-K filing cadence across the universe to gauge where negative sentiment may have over-corrected and where it remains unresolved. UNH's -19.6% earnings-day drop on 2026-01-27 was the most violent reaction in the group, followed by two director departure/appointment filings and a Reg FD disclosure through early March—this cluster of governance activity after a massive selloff suggests the narrative is still shifting and sentiment has not stabilized. MSFT's -10.0% post-earnings move on 2026-01-29 was severe but the filing trail has gone quiet since, which I read as the negative tone potentially being fully priced with no new catalysts to sustain it. AMZN stands out for the sheer volume of filings—four 8-Ks since its -5.6% earnings drop, including a material definitive agreement and multiple 'Other Events' filings in March—suggesting an evolving story that keeps media and analyst attention elevated and sentiment unsettled. CAT (+3.4%) and AAPL (+0.5%) had benign post-earnings reactions and minimal subsequent filing activity, consistent with stable-to-positive tone that I see as already reflected in price.

views.note: The -19.6% earnings selloff combined with three subsequent governance-related filings through March signals ongoing narrative instability and unresolved negative sentiment.
The -10.0% post-earnings drop was sharp but the absence of follow-on filings suggests the negative tone has been fully absorbed, creating a potential mean-reversion setup.
Four 8-K filings since the -5.6% earnings drop—including a material agreement and multiple 'Other Events'—keep the narrative unsettled and sentiment noisy.
The +3.4% post-earnings reaction and clean filing trail point to positive sentiment that, while partly priced, reflects genuine fundamental strength.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and a routine shareholder-vote filing suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment—no edge either way.
The -5.5% earnings drop was notable but two director-related filings (not operational) cloud the read; sentiment is negative but governance noise makes conviction low.
A mild -0.5% earnings reaction and subsequent director change filing suggest no strong sentiment signal in either direction.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices and Elevated Policy Uncertainty Signal Structural Geopolitical Stress Across the Universe
memos.body: I am reading the macro backdrop as one of acute geopolitical strain: WTI crude has surged 69% over three months to $96.11/bbl, the VIX is up 61% over the same window to 24.06, and the economic policy uncertainty index sits at 372—still elevated despite a one-month pullback. High-yield spreads have widened 37 bp over three months to 3.27%, while the 10y-2y curve has flattened 22 bp, consistent with markets pricing both policy risk and slower growth. I interpret the oil spike as likely driven by supply-side disruption—sanctions enforcement, OPEC+ discipline, or conflict-related outages—rather than demand strength, given the simultaneous credit deterioration. My highest conviction call is that energy names benefit structurally while hardware-intensive tech with China supply-chain exposure (AAPL, NVDA) faces the most policy headwind; a de-escalation in Middle East tensions or a rollback of export controls would change my view on both sides.

views.note: WTI at $96 with a 69% three-month surge directly lifts XOM's upstream margins; energy security policy tailwinds remain intact.
Elevated policy uncertainty and the ongoing tightening of semiconductor export controls to China create structural demand-side risk for NVDA's data-center GPU pipeline.
Supply-chain concentration in China and rising geopolitical friction make AAPL vulnerable to any escalation in tariffs or export restrictions.
CAT benefits from infrastructure spending but faces margin pressure from elevated input costs tied to the oil surge; net effect is roughly balanced.
Widening credit spreads and curve flattening offset any trading-desk volatility gains; geopolitical risk is a wash for large-bank earnings near term.
Multiple 8-K filings suggest active corporate maneuvering, but AMZN's domestic demand orientation partially insulates it from trade-policy risk; energy costs are the main headwind.
Defensive consumer staples with global pricing power tend to outperform in high-uncertainty, high-oil environments; PG fits that profile.
